title: Plugin Architecture in Practice(Part 2) - Contract, Registration, and Resolution - Debugging Life
snippet: A plugin architecture modularizes an application by defining stable contracts (interfaces) and loading external assemblies that implement those contracts at runtime. Contract stability is critical—your plugin interface is a public API, and once plugins are built against it, changing it breaks those plugins.
claim: An extension point is a public API; without versioning discipline the enhancement freedom is bought back with breakage.

query: Model Context Protocol specification version negotiation capabilities backwards compatibility 2026
title: Versioning - Model Context Protocol
snippet: In the current 2026-07-28 specification, the version is declared per request instead of negotiated once per session like in 2025-11-25 and earlier. More specifically, every request declares its protocol version through the io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion key in its _meta field — carried on Streamable HTTP as the MCP-Protocol-Version header. Deprecated features remain in the specification for at least twelve months.
claim: MCP 2026-07-28 declares protocol version per request with a 12-month deprecation window — a concrete versioned-interface discipline to copy.

title: GitHub - agentskills/agentskills: Specification and documentation for Agent Skills
snippet: Agent Skills are an open standard for packaging reusable workflows, domain expertise, and new capabilities into portable folders that any AI agent can discover and use. Every skill follows the same structure with a required SKILL.md file (YAML frontmatter + markdown instructions) plus optional scripts/, references/, and assets/ directories.
claim: Agent Skills is a portable capability-packaging standard that adds capability without modifying the agent runtime.
